_readme: Round 5 of 7 — big august 9th batch (in-copyright PDFs). Synopses grounded in real detect.mjs-extracted text; mentions curated from candidates.json per docs/detector.md exclusion rules; genres per tools/genres.mjs. Several titles (The Charioteer, The Death of Ivan Ilyich, The Last of the Wine, The Magic Mountain) backfill pre-existing metadata-less stubs.

books.title: The Anatomy Lesson
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: Novelist Nathan Zuckerman, crippled by unexplained chronic neck and shoulder pain and unable to write since publishing his notorious novel Carnovsky, is cared for by four women while feuding bitterly with his brother Henry and obsessing over a scathing critical essay by Milton Appel. Unable to work and convinced he wants a different life, he flies to Chicago posing as a pornography publisher to enroll in medical school, gets into a drunken graveside brawl that shatters his jaw, and ends up hospitalized, trailing interns on their rounds as a patient fascinated by real physical suffering.

books.title: The Breast
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: David Kepesh, a 38-year-old literature professor, narrates from a hospital bed after his body has transformed into a giant female breast; he recounts the onset of the transformation, sessions with his psychiatrist Dr. Klinger and nurse Miss Clark, and visits from his father, girlfriend Claire, and colleague Arthur Schonbrunn, while wrestling with whether his fate is a hallucination and whether it was inspired by the Kafka and Gogol stories he taught.

books.title: The Bull from the Sea
books.author: Mary Renault
books.synopsis: Narrated by Theseus in first person, the novel opens with his return to Athens after killing the Minotaur in Crete, and follows his kingship, his bond with Pirithoos, his abduction of the Amazon Hippolyta and her death defending Athens at his side, and his marriage to Phaedra whose passion for his son Hippolytos leads to the young man's death and Theseus's own ruin.

books.title: The Castle of Crossed Destinies
books.author: Italo Calvino
books.synopsis: A traveler takes shelter in a castle where an enchanted forest has struck all the guests mute, so they can only tell their life stories by laying out and pointing to tarot cards from a shared deck, producing tangled, overlapping tales—an ingrate's punishment, an alchemist's bargain, a doomed bride, a grave-robber, Roland driven mad with love, Astolpho's flight to the moon—that the narrator and others must piece together from the spread; a second part, 'The Tavern of Crossed Destinies,' repeats the device with a different deck, and a closing note describes Calvino's own struggle to construct both sections as a 'machine for constructing stories' out of the tarot images.

books.title: The Charioteer
books.author: Mary Renault
books.synopsis: Laurie Odell, wounded and evacuated from Dunkirk, recovers in a wartime English hospital while reconnecting with Ralph Lanyon, the older schoolmate who once gave him a copy of Plato's Phaedrus, and falling for Andrew, a conscientious-objector orderly; the novel traces Laurie's divided loyalties and his effort to reconcile the Phaedrus's ideal of love with the messy realities of his own life.

books.title: The Crossing
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
books.synopsis: Teenage brothers Billy and Boyd Parham cross from their New Mexico ranch into Mexico, first to return a trapped she-wolf to the mountains and later after their parents are killed, encountering a devastated hacienda, an itinerant opera troupe, and the loss of Boyd along the way before Billy makes a final solitary crossing.

books.title: The Dark Forest
books.author: Cixin Liu
books.synopsis: Facing an incoming Trisolaran invasion fleet, the UN's Planetary Defense Council names four Wallfacers—including sociologist Luo Ji—to devise secret defense strategies hidden even from their own species, since Trisolaris's sophons can monitor all human communication but not thought; Luo Ji eventually formulates the "dark forest" theory of cosmic civilizations as a deterrent, while political commissar Zhang Beihai maneuvers within the emerging Space Force and Earth's three star fleets are wiped out when they encounter a single Trisolaran probe.

books.title: The Death of Ivan Ilyich
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.synopsis: After the sudden death of Ivan Ilych Golovin, a Court of Justice official, his colleagues react with thoughts of promotions rather than grief, and the story traces back through Ivan Ilych's conventional rise through the legal bureaucracy to the mysterious illness that slowly kills him, isolating him in physical agony and existential dread until, in his final hours, he finds a strange peace.

books.title: The Diamond Age
books.author: Neal Stephenson
books.synopsis: In a nanotech-saturated future of tribal enclaves and floating city-states, a stolen interactive book called the Young Lady's Illustrated Primer raises a poor Shanghai girl named Nell while its engineer, its ruthless commissioner, and a Confucian judge in the Leased Territories are drawn into the fallout of its theft.

books.title: The Duniazat
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.synopsis: In 1195 Cordoba, the exiled philosopher Ibn Rushd (Averroes) takes in an orphaned girl named Dunia who is secretly a jinn princess, fathers a multitude of earlobe-less children with her during his internal exile, and abandons her and the children (nicknamed the Duniazat) when he is recalled to court after the Almohad victory at Alarcos; the story then traces how her descendants, ignorant of their supernatural origin, spread across the world over the following centuries.

books.title: The Facts: A Novelist's Autobiography
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: Philip Roth frames his own memoir as a letter to his fictional alter ego Nathan Zuckerman, tracing his Newark boyhood, his father's near-fatal 1944 surgery, his years at Bucknell and Chicago, his troubled first marriage to Josie, and the furor over his early Jewish-themed stories, then closes with a fictional Zuckerman letter that skeptically dissects the manuscript and urges Roth not to publish it.

books.title: The Fall
books.author: Albert Camus
books.synopsis: In an Amsterdam sailors' bar, the self-declared "judge-penitent" Jean-Baptiste Clamence delivers a rambling confession to a stranger, recounting his fall from a celebrated, self-satisfied Parisian lawyer into guilt after he failed to help a young woman who jumped into the Seine, and the corrosive philosophy of universal judgment he built from that failure.

books.title: The Ghost Writer
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: In 1956, young writer Nathan Zuckerman spends an evening at the Berkshires farmhouse of his literary idol E. I. Lonoff, where he becomes fixated on Amy Bellette, a mysterious young woman in the Lonoff household, and privately imagines she may secretly be Anne Frank, while witnessing Lonoff's wife Hope unravel and finally leave.

books.title: The Golden House
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.synopsis: Narrated by a young filmmaker neighbor, René, the novel follows Nero Golden and his three sons as they arrive in a Greenwich Village enclave on the day of a new president's inauguration to escape a hidden past in Bombay, and traces the family's unraveling over the following years of secrets, madness, and betrayal, ending in a fire that consumes the Golden house.

books.title: The Humbling
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: Aging stage actor Simon Axler loses his ability to act after a string of onstage failures, including a disastrous Macbeth, and suffers a breakdown; after a subsequent affair with a much younger woman, Pegeen, collapses, he stages his own suicide as a reenactment of the final line of Chekhov's The Seagull.

books.title: The Innocence of Objects
books.author: Orhan Pamuk
books.synopsis: Pamuk's nonfiction catalogue of his Museum of Innocence in Istanbul, walking through the museum's vitrines box by box while recounting how he collected everyday objects (Hilton Hotel postcards, matchbooks, photographs) to build the museum alongside his novel, and reflecting on the psychology of collecting, waiting, and time.

books.title: The King Must Die
books.author: Mary Renault
books.synopsis: Narrated in first person by Theseus, the novel follows him from his boyhood in Troizen, where he is raised believing himself fathered by a god, through his journey to Athens and his selection as one of the youths sent as tribute to Crete, where he trains as a bull-dancer in the Bull Court of Knossos Palace under the rule of the Cretan priest-queens.

books.title: The Last White Man
books.author: Mohsin Hamid
books.synopsis: In an unnamed town, a white man named Anders wakes to find his skin has turned dark brown, and as the same transformation spreads to others, the community descends into fear and militant violence before gradually, over years, accepting a world where everyone has changed color. The novel follows Anders and his partner Oona, and later their daughter, through this upheaval and its long aftermath.

books.title: The Last of the Wine
books.author: Mary Renault
books.synopsis: Narrated by Alexias, an Athenian youth who comes of age during the final years of the Peloponnesian War, the novel follows his education under Sokrates, his love for the older Lysis, and their shared endurance of famine, siege, and the terror of the Thirty Tyrants as Athens collapses toward defeat.

books.title: The Magic Mountain
books.author: Thomas Mann
books.synopsis: Young engineer Hans Castorp arrives at a Swiss Alpine sanatorium to visit his tubercular cousin Joachim, is himself diagnosed with a touch of the disease, and stays for seven years, drawn into a timeless world of illness, desire for the enigmatic Clavdia Chauchat, and prolonged ideological combat between the humanist Settembrini and the totalitarian ex-Jesuit Naphta, ending with Naphta's suicide and Castorp's departure into the First World War.

books.title: The Mask of Apollo
books.author: Mary Renault
books.synopsis: An Athenian tragic actor named Nikeratos narrates his career on the fourth-century BC theater circuit, from playing extras in his father's troupe to touring Sicily, where he becomes entangled with Dion of Syracuse and the philosopher Plato in their attempt to reform the tyranny of Dionysios II.

books.title: The Ministry of Utmost Happiness
books.author: Arundhati Roy
books.synopsis: The novel follows Anjum, a hijra who makes a home in a Delhi graveyard, and Tilo, a woman entangled with men on opposing sides of the Kashmir conflict, weaving together their stories with those of the Kashmiri insurgency, Gujarat's riots, and Delhi's protest movements.

books.title: The Moor's Account
books.author: Laila Lalami
books.synopsis: Mustafa ibn Muhammad, a Moroccan slave known to history only as Estevanico, narrates his own account of the disastrous 1527 Narvaez expedition to Florida, correcting the official Spanish record as he and a handful of survivors are shipwrecked, enslaved by various tribes, and wander for years across North America seeking a way back to freedom.

books.title: The Moor's Last Sigh
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.synopsis: Moraes 'Moor' Zogoiby, born with a withered hand and aging at twice the normal rate, tells the saga of his Cochin spice-trading family, dominated by his painter mother Aurora, tracing four generations of Indian history from colonial Malabar through Bombay's criminal underworld.

books.title: The Museum of Innocence
books.author: Orhan Pamuk
books.synopsis: Kemal, a wealthy Istanbul businessman engaged to marry a woman of his own class, falls obsessively in love with his poor distant cousin Fusun, and after losing her spends years amassing objects connected to her that he eventually assembles into the museum of the title.
